//: deploy/tailscale/acl-snippet.json — merge these keys into the tailnet's
policy file (Tailscale admin console -> Access Controls). Not a
standalone policy: it omits everything unrelated to this host.
Effect: only the owner's own identity may reach this host's dashboard
(443) and preview (8443) ports (docs/security.md C1, ADR 0002 'A
tailnet ACL further restricts the service to the owner's own identity,
as defense in depth beyond the app-level identity check'). Replace
OWNER_LOGIN with the Tailscale login you open the dashboard with (the
same value given to the wizard as `owner_login`, C2).
GRANTS ARE ADDITIVE: this grant restricts nothing on its own. A new
tailnet's default policy allows everything ({"src":["*"],"dst":["*"],
"ip":["*"]} in `grants`, or an `acls` rule {"action":"accept",
"src":["*"],"dst":["*:*"]}). Remove that rule, or narrow it so no
src other than OWNER_LOGIN reaches tag:pdash; otherwise every tailnet
device can still reach the dashboard.
The `tests` block makes the admin console reject a policy that breaks
this: replace OTHER_LOGIN with any other user (or tag) in your tailnet,
or delete that entry if you are its only user, and verify by hand from
a non-owner device instead (docs/setup.md step 3).
Tag the dashboard host itself with tag:pdash (preferably in the admin
console, Machines -> Edit ACL tags; or `tailscale up
--advertise-tags=tag:pdash`) so this grant follows the host even if its
hostname changes.
Funnel must stay off for this host (verified by
deploy/tailscale/serve.sh). Also drop any `funnel` entry in `nodeAttrs`
that would match this host, so nobody on it can turn Funnel on.
